en: Majjhima Nikāya 88,
the Bāhitikasutta:
Thus have I heard—
On one occasion the Blessed One was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Then, in the morning, the Venerable Ānanda dressed, took his bowl and robe, and entered Sāvatthī for alms.
Having walked for alms in Sāvatthī, after his meal, returning from his almsround, he approached the Eastern Monastery, Migāra’s Mother’s Mansion, for his midday rest.
Now at that time, King Pasenadi of Kosala, having mounted the elephant Ekapuṇḍarīka, was departing from Sāvatthī during the middle of the day.
King Pasenadi of Kosala saw the Venerable Ānanda coming from afar.
Having seen him, he addressed the chief minister Sirivaḍḍha:
“This venerable one, my good Sirivaḍḍha, is Ānanda.
“Yes, Great King, this venerable one is Ānanda.
Then King Pasenadi of Kosala addressed a certain man:
“Come, good man, go to where the Venerable Ānanda is; having approached him, pay homage with your head at the feet of the Venerable Ānanda in my name, saying:
‘Venerable sir, King Pasenadi of Kosala pays homage with his head at the feet of the Venerable Ānanda,’ and speak thus:”
“If, venerable sir, there is no urgent business for the Venerable Ānanda, may the Venerable Ānanda please wait a moment out of compassion.
“Very well, sire,” that man replied to King Pasenadi of Kosala, and he went to the Venerable Ānanda.
Having approached, he paid homage to the Venerable Ānanda and stood to one side. Standing to one side…
Standing there, that man said this to the Venerable Ānanda:
"Venerable sir, King Pasenadi of Kosala pays homage with his head at the feet of the Venerable Ānanda and says this:"
“If, venerable sir, there is no urgent business for the Venerable Ānanda, may the Venerable Ānanda please wait a moment out of compassion.
The Venerable Ānanda consented by remaining silent.
Then King Pasenadi of Kosala proceeded by elephant as far as the ground was suitable for an elephant; having descended from the elephant, he...
He approached the Venerable Ānanda on foot; having approached and paid homage to the Venerable Ānanda, he stood to one side.
Standing to one side, King Pasenadi of Kosala said this to the Venerable Ānanda:
"If, venerable sir, the Venerable Ānanda has no urgent business, it would be well, venerable sir, if the Venerable Ānanda would approach the bank of the river Aciravatī out of compassion."
The Venerable Ānanda consented by remaining silent.
Then the Venerable Ānanda approached the bank of the river Aciravatī; having arrived, he sat down on a seat prepared at the foot of a certain tree.
Then King Pasenadi of Kosala proceeded by elephant as far as the ground was passable for an elephant, and then dismounted from the elephant.
On foot, he approached the Venerable Ānanda; having approached and paid homage to the Venerable Ānanda, he stood to one side.
Standing to one side, King Pasenadi of Kosala said this to the Venerable Ānanda:
"Venerable sir, let the Venerable Ānanda sit here on the elephant rug."
“Enough, great king.
Sit down;
I am seated on my own seat.”
King Pasenadi of Kosala sat down on the prepared seat.
Having sat down, King Pasenadi of Kosala said this to the Venerable Ānanda:
"Venerable Ānanda, would the Blessed One engage in such bodily conduct as that which is subject to reproach by recluses and brahmins?"
“Great king, that Blessed One would not engage in such bodily conduct as would be subject to reproach by wise recluses and brahmins.
“But, venerable Ānanda, would that Blessed One engage in such verbal conduct...
[or] such mental conduct as would be subject to reproach by wise recluses and brahmins?”
“Indeed, Great King, that Blessed One would not engage in such mental conduct as would be subject to reproach by wise recluses and brahmins.
“It is wonderful, venerable sir! It is marvelous, venerable sir!
For that which we were unable to fulfill with our question has been fulfilled by the Venerable Ānanda through his answer.”
“Venerable sir, those who are foolish and incompetent, who speak of the praise or blame of others without investigating or scrutinizing, we do not accept that as being of substance.
But those who are wise, competent, and intelligent, who speak of the praise or blame of others after having investigated and scrutinized, we accept that as being of substance.
Venerable Ānanda, what kind of bodily conduct is subject to reproach by wise recluses and brahmins?”
“Great King, that bodily conduct which is unwholesome.
“But what, Bhante, is unwholesome bodily conduct?
“Great King, that bodily conduct which is blameworthy.”
“But what, venerable sir, is bodily conduct that is blameworthy?
“Any bodily conduct, great king, that is harmful.
“But what, venerable sir, is bodily conduct that is harmful?”
“Whatever bodily conduct, Great King, has a painful result.
“But what kind of bodily conduct, Bhante, has a painful result?
“Whatever bodily conduct, Great King, leads to one’s own affliction, leads to the affliction of others, and leads to the affliction of both.”
“His unwholesome states increase and his wholesome states decline.
Such bodily conduct, Great King, is censurable by wise recluses and brahmins.
“But what, venerable Ānanda, is verbal conduct...?”
“Is mental conduct censured by wise recluses and brahmins?
“Any mental conduct, Great King, that is unwholesome.
“But what, venerable sir, is unwholesome mental conduct?”
“Whatever mental conduct, Great King, is blameworthy.
“But what, Bhante, is blameworthy mental conduct?
“Whatever mental conduct, Great King, is accompanied by affliction.”
“But what, venerable sir, is mental conduct that is afflictive?
“Whatever mental conduct, Great King, has a painful ripening.
“But what, venerable sir, is mental conduct that has a painful ripening?”
“Whatever mental conduct, Great King, leads to one’s own affliction, leads to the affliction of others, and leads to the affliction of both—
unwholesome states increase for such a person and wholesome states decline.
Such mental conduct, Great King, is subject to reproach by wise recluses and brahmins.”
“Venerable Ānanda, does that Blessed One praise the abandoning of all unwholesome states?
“Great King, the Tathāgata has indeed abandoned all unwholesome states and is endowed with wholesome states.
“But what kind of bodily conduct, venerable Ānanda, is beyond reproach by wise recluses and brahmins?”
“Whatever bodily conduct, Great King, is wholesome.
“But what, Bhante, is wholesome bodily conduct?
“That bodily conduct, Great King, which is blameless.”
“But what, venerable sir, is bodily conduct that is blameless?
“Any bodily conduct, great king, that is free from affliction.
“But what, venerable sir, is bodily conduct that is free from affliction?”
“Whatever bodily conduct, Great King, has a pleasant result.
“But what, Bhante, is bodily conduct that has a pleasant result?
“That bodily conduct, Great King, which leads neither to one’s own affliction, nor to the affliction of others, nor to the affliction of both.”
“His unwholesome states diminish and his wholesome states increase.
Such bodily conduct, Great King, is beyond reproach by wise recluses and brahmins.
“But what, venerable Ānanda, is verbal conduct...?”
“Is mental conduct irreproachable by wise recluses and brahmins?
“Any mental conduct that is wholesome, Great King.
“But what, venerable sir, is wholesome mental conduct?”
“Whatever mental conduct, great king, is blameless.
“But what, venerable sir, is blameless mental conduct?
“Whatever mental conduct, great king, is non-afflictive.”
“But what, venerable sir, is mental conduct that is blameless?
“Whatever mental conduct, Great King, has a pleasant ripening.
“But what, venerable sir, is mental conduct that has a pleasant ripening?”
“Whatever mental conduct, Great King, leads neither to one’s own affliction, nor to the affliction of others, nor to the affliction of both—
therein unwholesome states diminish and wholesome states increase.
Such mental conduct, Great King, is beyond reproach by wise recluses and brahmins.”
“But, venerable Ānanda, does that Blessed One praise the full attainment of all wholesome states?
“Great King, the Tathāgata has abandoned all unwholesome states and is endowed with all wholesome states.
“It is wonderful, venerable sir! It is marvelous, venerable sir!”
"How well spoken this was, Bhante, by the Venerable Ānanda!
We are uplifted and delighted, Bhante, by this well-spoken word of the Venerable Ānanda.
Indeed, we are uplifted and delighted, Bhante, by this well-spoken word of the Venerable Ānanda."
“Venerable sir, if the elephant-treasure were suitable for the venerable Ānanda, we would give the elephant-treasure to the venerable Ānanda.
Venerable sir, if the horse-treasure were suitable for the venerable Ānanda, we would give the horse-treasure to the venerable Ānanda.
Venerable sir, if a choice village were suitable for the venerable Ānanda, we would give that choice village to the venerable Ānanda.”
Moreover, venerable sir, we know this:
"This is not allowable for the Venerable Ānanda.
Venerable sir, this cloak of mine was sent by King Ajātasattu Vedehiputta of Magadha, having been placed inside a tube; it is sixteen spans in length and eight spans in width.
“Venerable sir, may the Venerable Ānanda accept it out of compassion.
“Enough, great king; my triple robe is complete.
“Venerable sir, this River Aciravatī has been seen by both the Venerable Ānanda and by us.”
When a great cloud has rained down upon the mountain above, then this River Aciravatī flows along, overflowing both its banks;
even so, venerable sir, the Venerable Ānanda will make his own triple robe from this cloak.
As for the Venerable Ānanda’s former triple robe, he will share it with his fellow celibates.
"In this way, our gift will seem to flow forth as it goes," [he said].
"Venerable sir, may the Venerable Ānanda accept the cloak.
The Venerable Ānanda accepted the cloak.
Then King Pasenadi of Kosala said to the Venerable Ānanda:
"Well now, venerable Ānanda, let us go;
we have many duties and much to do."
“Now, Great King, you may go at whatever time you deem appropriate.

Then King Pasenadi of Kosala, having rejoiced and expressed his appreciation for the Venerable Ānanda’s words, rose from his seat, paid homage to the Venerable Ānanda, and keeping him to his right, departed.
Not long after King Pasenadi of Kosala had left, the Venerable Ānanda approached the Blessed One; having approached, he paid homage to the Blessed One and sat down to one side.
Seated to one side, the Venerable Ānanda reported to the Blessed One the entirety of his conversation with King Pasenadi of Kosala,
and he presented that cloak to the Blessed One.
Then the Blessed One addressed the bhikkhus:
“It is a gain, monks, for King Pasenadi of Kosala; it is a great gain for King Pasenadi of Kosala, that he obtains the sight of Ānanda and obtains the opportunity to attend upon him.
Thus spoke the Blessed One.
Delighted, those bhikkhus rejoiced in the Blessed One’s words.
The eighth discourse, the Bāhitikasutta, is concluded.
